# Judith Chapter 1 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1:1** In the twelfth year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, who ruled over the Assyrians in Nineveh the great city — in those days Arphaxad was ruling over the Medes in Ecbatana.

**1:2** Arphaxad had built walls around Ecbatana of hewn stones three cubits thick and six cubits long, and he made the wall's height seventy cubits and its breadth fifty cubits.

**1:3** At its gates he set towers one hundred cubits high, sixty cubits wide at their base.

**1:4** He made its gates seventy cubits high and forty cubits wide, for the going out of his mighty armies and the marshaling of his infantry.

**1:5** In those days King Nebuchadnezzar made war against King Arphaxad on the great plain on the borders of Ragae.

**1:6** All the inhabitants of the hill country rallied to him, as did all who dwelt beside the Euphrates and the Tigris and the Hydaspes and on the plain of Arioch king of the Elymaeans. Many peoples of the sons of Cheloud gathered together and took their stand for battle.

**1:7** Then Nebuchadnezzar king of the Assyrians sent word to all who dwelt in Persia and to all who dwelt in the west — to those in Cilicia and Damascus and Lebanon and Anti-Lebanon, and to all who dwelt along the seacoast,

**1:8** to the peoples of Carmel and Gilead and Upper Galilee and the great plain of Esdraelon,

**1:9** and to all those in Samaria and its cities, and beyond the Jordan as far as Jerusalem and Betane and Chelous and Kadesh and the river of Egypt, and Tahpanhes and Rameses and all the land of Goshen,

**1:10** even as far as Tanis and Memphis, and to all who inhabited Egypt to the borders of Ethiopia.

**1:11** But all the inhabitants of the land disregarded the word of Nebuchadnezzar king of the Assyrians and did not join him on the campaign, for they had no fear of him. He seemed to them like a single man of no account, and they sent his messengers back empty-handed and in disgrace.

**1:12** Then Nebuchadnezzar was exceedingly angry with all this land, and he swore by his throne and his kingdom that he would surely take vengeance on all the territories of Cilicia and Damascus and Syria — putting to the sword all who dwelt in the land of Moab and among the Ammonites and throughout Judea and all who were in Egypt, as far as the borders of the two seas.

**1:13** In the seventeenth year he drew up his forces against King Arphaxad and prevailed in the battle. He overthrew the entire force of Arphaxad, all his cavalry and all his chariots,

**1:14** and became master of his cities. He came to Ecbatana, captured its towers, plundered its marketplaces, and turned its glory into shame.

**1:15** He captured Arphaxad in the mountains of Ragae, ran him through with his spears, and utterly destroyed him on that day.

**1:16** Then he returned with all his company — a very great mixed multitude of fighting men — and there he rested and feasted, he and his army, for one hundred and twenty days.
